To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dopaminergic system activation by dopaminergic receptor agonists, acting through the tuberoinundibular or meso-limbic pathways, causes a significant change in the activity and protein levels of cytochrome P-450 isoforms and hormones in the liver, and this effect is accompanied by a change in the level of cytokines.

the activation of brain dopaminerergic system by dopamine or apomorphine, amphetamine and quinpiroline, respectively, causes a rise in CYP2B and 3A protein levels and activities in the liver, a decrease in CYP1A protein levels and activity, and a rise in corticosterone and growth hormone levels.

activation of dopaminergic system in the pituitaries and nucleus accumbens by dopaminergic agonists and amphetamine, but not by SKF82958 (D(1) receptor-specific agonist), results in the up-regulation of the liver CYP2B and CYP3a isoforms, and in the down-regulation of the CYP1A isoform.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel physiological mechanism controlling liver CYP expression and a new pharmacological aspect of dopaminomimetic drugs.

the identification of new factors regulating the activity and expression of CYP isoforms in liver and may contribute to the understanding of the role of dopaminergic system in the pathogenesis of some liver diseases
the influence of the dopaminergic system activation on CYP expression in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dopaminergic stimulation of the brain induces changes in the level of liver CYP isoforms, which may have an impact on the pharmacokinetics of drugs and on their toxicity.

dopaminergic system, by activation of D(2) dopamine receptors, is involved in the regulation of CYP2C, CYP3A and CYP1A activities and that the effect is mediated through pituitary hormones (GH and T(3)) and corticosterone.

the brain dopaminomimetic compounds, which activate the tuberoinfudibular or meso-limbic pathways, are capable of inducing a substantial change in CYP2B and CYP2C, a moderate change in CYP3 and CYP1A and a significant change in the blood plasma levels of GH and corticosterone, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
activation of the tuberohypothalamic dopaminergic system, via D(2) dopaminoceptors in the pituitaries, leads to an increased expression of CYP2C and CYP3 isoforms in the liver.
activation of dopaminergic system in the brain causes a rise in CYP2B/C11/3A activities and protein levels and a drop in CYP1A levels in liver.
dopaminergic system, through its interaction with pituitary hormones and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, regulates the activity of cytochrome P-450 isoforms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activation of brain dopaminoceptive pathways by dopaminergic agonists may lead to the development of new pharmacological approaches to the modulation of liver CYP expression.

activation of the dopaminergic system in the brain can be a useful pharmacological approach in the treatment of liver diseases, including those related to CYP isoform imbalance, and in the development of new drugs.

activation of the dopaminergic system in the brain by dopaminergic agonists may lead to changes in the level and activity in liver CYPs, and that this may have important pharmacological and toxicological implications.
